topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence
target_audience: Advanced Undergraduate Physics or Engineering Students

sections.title: The Intuitive Paradox: Chaos vs. Structure
lecture_lines: Turbulence paradox: chaos meets underlying order.
Reynolds Number quantifies inertial vs. viscous forces.
Turbulence is an organized energy cascade.
animations: Fade in contrast: chaos vs. structure.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Cascade: Mathematical Scaling
lecture_lines: Richardson proposed energy cascades through scales.
Energy dissipates at the smallest scales.
Spectrum E(k) follows power law slope.

sections.title: The Universal Constant: Kolmogorov’s C
lecture_lines: Physics remains independent of specific fluid.
Inertial range shows stable universal behavior.
Log-Log plot reveals consistent power law.
Constants define the structure across environments.
animations: Show C independent of flow scale #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Closure Problem & Mathematical Structure
lecture_lines: We use statistical structure functions instead.
Equations exhibit spatial and temporal self-similarity.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Turbulence is statistically predictable via constants.
Constants advance climate and aerospace modeling.
Mathematical structure reveals nature's complex order.
